transcript.text: Thanks, Morgan. I need to report a significant safety concern. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. These errors occurred at the point of selection from the automated dispensing cabinets, where both concentrations are currently stocked side by side. Given the risk of a patient receiving the wrong concentration — which could lead to a serious dosing error with an intravenous anticoagulant — I'd recommend that pharmacy remove the bedside stock of both concentrations from the ADCs and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold. This would eliminate the selection risk at the cabinet level while we work through the safety review.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for these thorough and timely reports. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and outline my preliminary thinking before I make the final decision this afternoon.

First, Leah — three selection errors in just a few days at the ADC level is a serious signal. Your recommendation to remove both concentrations from bedside stock and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes is a strong candidate for a temporary safeguard.

Second, Ravi — the anti-Xa analyzer being unavailable until Friday at 17:00 means aPTT monitoring every six hours is our only approved lab pathway. That has implications for turnaround time and clinical interpretation that we need to account for.

Third, Tessa — 18 nurses without completed competency modules is a significant coverage risk for tonight. We need a plan to ensure safe administration coverage.

Fourth, Jon — the 16:00 EMR alert is a valuable system-level safeguard at the ordering stage, but it addresses ordering, not the physical selection at the cabinet that Leah identified.

Here's my preliminary thinking: I'm inclined to implement a temporary hold on ADC stocking of both concentrations, with pharmacy supplying only prepared 1 mg/mL syringes, combined with deployment of Jon's EMR alert at 16:00 as an additional ordering safeguard. For monitoring, we proceed with aPTT every six hours per the lab's approved replacement protocol. For nursing competency, I want to explore whether charge-nurse sign-off is feasible for all 18 nurses tonight or whether we need to limit protocol use to units with sufficient competent staffing. Before I finalize, I'd like to hear from each of you: are there any additional concerns or constraints I should factor in? Leah, can pharmacy support the volume of prepared syringes if we remove ADC stock? Ravi, are there any patients currently on the protocol whose monitoring would be affected? Tessa, is charge-nurse sign-off realistic for 18 nurses before tonight's shift? Jon, are there any dependencies or risks with deploying the alert at 16:00?

transcript.text: Thanks, Morgan. To answer your question about pharmacy supporting the volume of prepared syringes — yes, pharmacy can support supplying only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold. We have the staffing and compounding capacity to handle the inpatient volume, and this approach would eliminate the selection risk at the cabinet level entirely. One additional consideration: by standardizing to a single concentration prepared by pharmacy, we also reduce the cognitive load on nursing at the point of administration, which may help with the competency gap Tessa identified. I don't have any further concerns beyond what I've already raised — the three selection errors I verified since Monday are the core issue, and removing both concentrations from ADC stock addresses that directly.

transcript.text: Thanks, Morgan. To answer your question about patients currently on the protocol — I don't have specific information about which patients are currently receiving the anticoagulant or when they started therapy. What I can confirm is that the laboratory's approved replacement monitoring pathway, aPTT every six hours, is ready to support any patients on the protocol starting now and through Friday at 17:00 when the anti-Xa analyzer becomes available for calibration. From a laboratory operations standpoint, we can handle the aPTT monitoring volume without issue. One consideration I'd flag for the group: aPTT-based monitoring requires clinical teams to be aware that the therapeutic range and interpretation differ from anti-Xa-based monitoring, so clear communication of the monitoring plan to treating clinicians will be important. I don't have any additional concerns beyond what I've already reported regarding the analyzer and the approved replacement protocol.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thanks, Morgan. To answer your question about whether charge-nurse sign-off is realistic for 18 nurses before tonight's shift — realistically, it is not. Charge nurses are already managing patient flow, admissions, discharges, and rapid responses. Expecting them to individually verify competency for 18 nurses before the shift begins would place an enormous burden on a role that is already stretched thin, and it risks either rushed sign-offs that compromise the integrity of the competency check or delays in patient care if nurses are blocked from administering the medication. I'd recommend we consider a more targeted approach: limit the protocol tonight to units that have a sufficient number of nurses who have already completed the competency module, and defer expansion to other units until the remaining nurses complete the training. This would protect patient safety without overloading charge nurses or creating coverage gaps. I'd also suggest we prioritize completing the module for those 18 nurses as quickly as possible so we're not in this position again for the next shift cycle.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on ADC stocking of both anticoagulant concentrations; pharmacy supplies only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the hold period.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Standardize to single pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL concentration only; remove both 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL from automated dispensing cabinets.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Proceed with aPTT monitoring every six hours as the approved replacement protocol until anti-Xa analyzer calibration is complete on Friday at 17:00. Ensure clear communication of aPTT therapeutic range and interpretation differences to treating clinicians.
decisions.nurse_authorization: Limit protocol use tonight to units with sufficient numbers of nurses who have already completed the competency module. Defer expansion to other units until the 18 untrained nurses complete the module. Charge-nurse sign-off for all 18 nurses tonight is not feasible.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the EMR concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today as an additional ordering-stage safeguard, complementary to the single-concentration dispensing approach.

Prioritize completion of the anticoagulant administration module for the 18 nurses who have not yet completed it, to enable protocol expansion to additional units for the next shift cycle.
Identify units with sufficient competency-completed nurses to support the protocol tonight and restrict protocol use to those units until competency gaps are closed.
